answers.meaning: Box, Flex, Stack/HStack/VStack, Grid, Simple Grid and Group share the focused styling set: spacing, dimensions, positioning, visibility, colors, borders, corners, shadows and parent placement.
answers.limits: Scope choice only; exact properties/types, native as sets and unverified behavior are not approved.

answers.meaning: Flex, Stack/HStack/VStack, Grid, Simple Grid and Group support Box's div/span/section/article/main/nav/aside/header/footer native set, div default, retaining flex/grid arrangement; span requires phrasing content.
answers.limits: Real wrapper geometry and accessible semantics require verification; no arbitrary as/asChild support or implementation approval.

answers.meaning: Peter requests matching Chakra's actual behavior; neither offered policy selected. Inspect source before deriving policy, distinguish React style inputs from house HTML JSON.
answers.sourceFinding: The pinned Chakra style pipeline derives styles from current props, skips nullish leaves, transforms token values or raw values, serializes CSS and replaces the generated class. It does not implement a last-valid-input store or universal CSS-value validation. JavaScript object inputs mean house HTML JSON decoding has no direct Chakra counterpart.
answers.direction: Follow Chakra's current-input CSS behavior for comparable style values; withdraw the previous last-valid-value recommendation. Do not automatically equate this with clearing every malformed input or with a universal development warning.
answers.unresolved: Malformed HTML JSON and structurally invalid house responsive data have no demonstrated Chakra equivalent. Keep a bounded converter-contract gap; do not infer user selection of either offered fallback.
answers.verification: Complete pinned source inspection of css.ts, serialize.ts, use-resolved-props.ts, utility.ts, system.ts, factory.tsx, conditions.ts, normalize.ts. No new browser run.

observations.finding: Computes current style inputs; no separate last-valid-value store.
Skips nullish leaves, transforms/merges current normalized CSS and sorts rules.
Token or raw input reaches per-property transform; no universal value validator here.
Property-name recognition and responsive-array normalization do not define house JSON behavior.
Current styles become serialized CSS and generated class supplied to the element.
Known-condition lookup retains unresolved names; no blanket house responsive validation contract.
